links.outcome: PE risk discrimination (AUC) of Copilot versus Wells score on same vignettes
links.effect: Copilot AUC 0.713 (P<0.001) versus Wells score AUC 0.583 (P=.091); Copilot risk levels significantly higher in PE patients.
links.quote: Copilot demonstrated better discriminatory power than the Wells score in risk assessment of PE (area under the curve 0.713 vs 0.583), with statistical significance (P<0.001 vs P=.091).

links.outcome: Inclusion of PE in differential diagnosis and sensitivity of high-risk categorization
links.effect: PE was in top-10 differential in 94.3% of cases; sensitivity for high-risk category was 34%, specificity 97.1%, NPV 59.6%.
links.quote: Copilot correctly included PE in the differential diagnosis in 94.3% of cases by listing it within the top 10 conditions.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4) performance on 140 clinical vignettes for pulmonary embolism diagnostic reasoning and risk assessment without evaluating specific deployment safeguards or practices.
